newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan money rates end higher on stocks, dollar.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan money rates end higher on stocks, dollar.

text.p: Taiwan's money rates closed higher on Tuesday amid tightening liquidity due to a sizzling stock market and depreciating Taiwan dollar, dealers said.
The overnight interbank rate ended at 6.859 percent against Monday's 6.761 close -- outside the central bank's 5.0-5.5 percent target zone but far below the record double-digit closes of late June.
The 30-day commercial paper jumped to 7.25 percent against 6.75-6.85.

Dealers said big turnover in the red-hot bourse intensified a flow of funds from the banking system, while the Taiwan dollar's fall below T$28 to the U.S. dollar sparked concerns the central bank may intervene to support the currency.

On Tuesday, the benchmark stock index surged to an intra-day peak of 10,057.95 in early trade, but lost steam in late session to finish at 9,892.34, down 30.71 points or 0.31 percent from Monday's close. Turnover was very heavy at T$224 billion.
The Taiwan dollar plunged below the central bank's long-time T$28 defence level to close at T$28.170, its lowest level in more than eight years.
Dealers said they expected the money rates to rise further in the near term.
In the bond market, the 10-year 86/4 bond yield edged higher at 6.0725.
